academic_translation:
Whichever Protectors of the World have passed and are in the ten directions,
And those who will appear in future times—they arise from this.
She is the Mother who gives birth to the Victors, the Teachers of the World,
And she reveals the mental conduct of other sentient beings.
translation: Think of every Protector of the World from the past and those in the ten directions right now. Those who will appear in the future also come from this. She is the Mother who gives birth to the Victorious Ones, the Teachers of the World. She also shows how other living beings think and act.

academic_translation:
The suchness of the world and the suchness of an arhat,
The suchness of a pratyekabuddha and the suchness of the children of the Victors,
Are one itself, devoid of entities, not other—they are suchness;
The Tathāgata knows the perfection of wisdom.

locked_terms.use: the way the world really is
the way things really are for worthy ones
the way things really are for a solitary Buddha
the way things really are for the children of the Victorious Ones

translation: Think of the way the world really is. Think of the way things really are for worthy ones. Think of the way things really are for a solitary Buddha, and the way things really are for the children of the Victorious Ones. All these are just one thing. They are free of real things, and they are not different. They are simply the way things really are. The Thus-Gone One knows the perfect wisdom.

academic_translation:
Whether the wise remain in the world or pass into nirvāṇa,
This flawless true nature of phenomena, the emptiness of phenomena, remains;
Bodhisattvas realize this suchness,
And therefore Buddhas are given the name Tathāgata.
translation: Wise people may stay in the world. They may pass into the peace beyond sorrow. Either way, the flawless true nature of things remains. This is the emptiness of things. An awakening hero realizes the way things really are. Because of this, a Buddha is called a Thus-Gone One.

academic_translation:
Relying on the perfection of wisdom as a pleasure grove,
The Guides with the ten powers have this as their domain;
Though they completely deliver sentient beings from suffering and the three lower realms,
They never have the perception of sentient beings.
translation: Guides with the ten powers rely on perfect wisdom as a beautiful garden. This is their home. They completely save living beings from suffering and the three lower realms. Even so, they never hold the idea of living beings.

academic_translation:
For example, just as a lion relying fearlessly on a mountain glen
Terrifies many small wild animals and lets out a roar,
The Lion among Men, relying on the perfection of wisdom,
Terrifies many non-Buddhists and also lets out a roar in the world.
translation: Think of a fearless lion resting in a mountain cave. It lets out a roar and scares many small wild animals. In the same way, the Lion among People relies on perfect wisdom. He lets out a roar in the world and scares many followers of another path.

academic_translation:
For example, just as the rays of the sun abiding in the sky
Dry up this earth and perfectly reveal forms,
Likewise, the Dharma King, relying on the perfection of wisdom,
Dries up the river of craving and perfectly teaches the Dharma.
translation: Think of the sun shining in the sky. Its rays dry up the earth and perfectly show all forms. In the same way, the King of the Teaching relies on perfect wisdom. He dries up the river of craving and strong wanting. He perfectly shows the teaching.

academic_translation:
One does not see forms, and one also does not see feelings,
One does not see perceptions, and one does not see volitions,
That in which consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen—
The Tathāgata taught that this is seeing the Dharma.
translation: You do not see forms. You do not see feelings. You do not see ideas. You do not see intentions. You do not see awareness, mind, or the thinking mind. The Thus-Gone One taught that this is seeing the teaching.

academic_translation:
Sentient beings express in words, "I see space,"
But how is space seen? Examine the meaning of this.
The Tathāgata taught that the seeing of phenomena is also like that;
This seeing cannot be described by any other example.
translation: Living beings say, "I see space." But how do you see space? Think about what this means. The Thus-Gone One taught that seeing things is just like that. This kind of seeing cannot be explained with any other example.

academic_translation:
Whoever sees in that way sees all phenomena.
Just as a king sits in equanimity while his ministers do everything,
Whatever deeds of the Buddhas and phenomena of the śrāvakas there are,
The perfection of wisdom does them all.
translation: Anyone who sees in this way sees all things. Think of a king who sits in calm balance while his helpers do everything. It is the same for the deeds of a Buddha and all the things of a listener. Perfect wisdom does them all.

academic_translation:
Just as a king does not go to villages or provinces,
Yet gathers all revenue from his own realm,
The true nature of phenomena of a bodhisattva does not go anywhere,
Yet gathers all the qualities of the stage of a Buddha.
translation: A king might not visit the towns and lands of his kingdom. But he still collects all the wealth from his country. The true nature of things for an awakening hero is like that. It does not go anywhere, but it gathers every good quality of the level of a Buddha.

academic_translation:
Whoever has firm faith in the Sugatas and bodhisattvas,
And has intention and application toward the supreme perfection of wisdom,
Having completely transcended the two stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas,
Will swiftly attain the unassailable awakening of the Victors.
translation: Some people have strong trust in the Well-Gone Ones and awakening heroes. They set their minds on the highest perfect wisdom. They will pass right by the two levels of the listener and the solitary Buddha. They will quickly reach the unbeatable awakening of the Victorious Ones.

academic_translation:
For example, when a boat entering the ocean breaks apart,
Whoever does not hold onto a corpse, grass, or wood,
Will perish in the middle of the water and will not reach the shore;
But whoever holds onto them will reach the far side of the ocean.
translation: Think of a boat that breaks apart on the ocean. A person in the water might not grab onto a dead body, grass, or floating wood. They will drown in the middle of the water and never reach the shore. But anyone who holds onto those things will reach the far side of the ocean.

academic_translation:
Likewise, whoever is endowed with faith and has obtained confidence,
But does not follow the Mother, the perfection of wisdom,
translation: In the same way, someone might be full of trust and gain confidence. But they might fail to follow the Mother, perfect wisdom.

academic_translation:
If their qualities of skillful means are fully embraced by wisdom,
They will swiftly reach the supremely wondrous awakening of the Sugatas.
translation: If the good qualities of their clever ways are fully guided by wisdom, they will quickly reach the wonderful awakening of the Well-Gone Ones.

academic_translation:
For example, if someone carries water in an unfired clay pot,
One should know that, being fragile, it will quickly break.
When carrying water in a fired pot, there is no fear of it breaking on the way,
And, without breaking, it will safely arrive home.
translation: Think about carrying water in an unbaked clay pot. It is weak and will break quickly. But a baked clay pot will not break on the way. The water will reach your home safely.

academic_translation:
Likewise, even if a bodhisattva has much faith,
If they are bereft of wisdom, they will quickly fall to ruin.
If their faith is fully embraced by wisdom,
Having entirely transcended the two stages, they will attain supreme awakening.
translation: In the same way, an awakening hero might have a lot of trust. But without wisdom, they will quickly fail. If their trust is guided by wisdom, they will succeed. They will go past the two levels and reach the highest awakening.

academic_translation:
For example, a boat that is not well constructed in the ocean
Will be destroyed along with its wealth and its merchants.
If that boat has been well constructed,
It will not be destroyed and will reach the shore along with its wealth.
translation: Think of a badly built boat on the ocean. It will break apart and sink with all its treasure and merchants. But a well-built boat will stay safe. It will reach the shore with all its treasure.

academic_translation:
Likewise, even if a bodhisattva is fully imbued with faith,
If they lack wisdom, they will quickly fall away from awakening.
If they possess the supreme perfection of wisdom,
Unharmed and undiminished, they will touch the awakening of the Victors.
translation: In the same way, an awakening hero might be full of trust. But without wisdom, they will quickly fall away from awakening. If they have the highest perfect wisdom, they will stay safe. They will reach the awakening of the Victorious Ones.

academic_translation:
A person who is a hundred and twenty years old, aged and suffering,
Even if they stand up, is unable to walk on their own.
If they are supported by people on both the left and the right,
They will proceed with ease, without the fear of falling.
translation: Imagine a person who is a hundred and twenty years old, very old and in pain. Even if they stand up, they cannot walk alone. But if people hold them up on both sides, they can walk easily. They do not need to fear falling.

academic_translation:
Likewise, a bodhisattva whose power of wisdom is weak,
Even if they set out, will completely fall away.
If they are fully embraced by skillful means and supreme wisdom,
They will not fall away, and will touch the awakening of a Tathāgata.
translation: In the same way, an awakening hero might have weak wisdom. Even if they start their journey, they will fall away. But if they are supported by clever ways and great wisdom, they will stay safe. They will reach the awakening of a Thus-Gone One.

academic_translation:
Those bodhisattvas who abide on the stage of a beginner,
And have set out for the supreme awakening of a Buddha with a superior intention,
Those excellent students possessing devotion to their master
Should always rely upon wise masters.
translation: Some awakening heroes are on the level of a beginner. They set out for the highest awakening of a Buddha with a strong aim. These excellent students are devoted to their teacher. They should always rely on wise teachers.

academic_translation:
Why is that? The qualities of the wise arise from them;
They teach the perfection of wisdom.
"The qualities of a Buddha depend upon the spiritual friend"—
So spoke the Victor, who possesses the supreme of all qualities.
translation: Why is that? The good qualities of the wise come from these teachers. They teach perfect wisdom. The Victorious One has the highest of all good qualities. He said, "A Buddha's qualities depend on the wise friend."

academic_translation:
"Dedicate generosity, ethical discipline, patience, and likewise diligence,
Meditative concentration, and wisdom to awakening!
Do not harbor clinging to the supreme by being attached to the aggregates of awakening!"—
Thus should it be taught to the beginner.
translation: This is how you should teach a beginner. Tell them, "Dedicate generosity, good conduct, patience, and steady effort to awakening! Dedicate deep focus and wisdom to awakening, too! Do not hold on to the heaps of awakening. Do not have any clinging to the supreme!"

academic_translation:
Those who practice thus, who are oceans of goodness and moons among speakers,
Are the refuge, the defender, and the dwelling place of beings;
They are the support, the intellect, the island, and Guides seeking their welfare,
Illuminators, lamps, and imperturbable speakers of the supreme Dharma.
translation: Those who practice like this are oceans of goodness. They are moons among speakers. They are the refuge, the defender, and the dwelling place for beings. They are the support, the mind, and the island. They are Guides who help everyone. They are bright lamps who stay completely calm. They speak the highest teaching.

These famous heroes put on armor for hard deeds. This is not the armor of the heaps, elements, and sense doors. They are free from the idea of the three vehicles. They have no holding on. They are never turning back. They never waver, and their nature is perfectly calm.

They have these qualities and are free from tangled thinking. They are free from doubt, hesitation, and unsure minds. They hold the true meaning. When they hear perfect wisdom, they do not shrink back. They do not rely on others. You should know them as never turning back.

academic_translation:
This Dharma of the Guides is profound and difficult to see;
It is not realized by anyone, nor is there any attaining of it.
Therefore, the Compassionate Benefactor, having attained awakening,
Felt little inclination, thinking, "Who among the masses of sentient beings will understand?"
translation: This teaching of the Guides is deep and hard to see. No one can just figure it out or reach it. So, when the Kind Helper reached awakening, he paused. He thought, "Who among all the living beings will understand this?"

Living beings love their dwelling places. They want the things we sense. Foolish people keep holding on, lost in darkness. But the teaching to reach has no dwelling place. It involves no holding on. This is why it clashes with the world.
